_: What the change-plane loop has learned from Mac's notes (graph-engineering-loop). Each rule: what he said, the rule behind it, and every place it was carried to.

rules.said: the chronicle tab is clearly off screen; I had to scroll
rules.rule: Check every panel on Mac's 1920x1080 display at scale 0.96, not only on the retina screen. Panels fit their content without scrolling when they can.

rules.said: look at the top studio houses and think how they do things
rules.rule: Copy a named big-studio screen: the command card's large keys with hotkeys in the corners (Warcraft III, Age of Empires IV), the quest tracker under the date (Anno 1800).

rules.said: this looks a bit weird (the strip unfolding on hover)
rules.rule: Nothing changes width or position on hover. Show the figures always or put them in a tooltip.
A row of actions in a table is a row of icon keys, with the name and price in the tooltip, never stacked words that make the row tall.

rules.said: this is taking more space than it needs to
rules.rule: A list item is one line: the figure, then what it's doing. Its place goes to the tooltip unless the place is the news.

rules.said: at least needs to be center aligned
rules.rule: A group of keys sits centred in its slot, never hung from the top.

rules.said: IDK what this means (March on a town: relieve it or besiege it)
rules.rule: A goal names its place and its foe: 'Take Gildport from House Goldcrest', never 'a town'. Two orders that look alike are told apart by name.

rules.said: how come there is only one option here?
rules.rule: A matter offers every answer its words name (stop it, sit it out, wed them), and names none it can't give.

rules.said: the 3 promises should be checkboxes, and I should be able to action them
rules.rule: Every goal on screen is a checkbox that says its state by shape and word, and a click goes where it's kept.

rules.said: a compact version of houses on the screen: who is gaining power, who is with me, who is against me
rules.rule: The houses are always on screen as a compact strip: stance word (sworn, warm, cold, at war), power and its trend; a click opens the full house.
